system.name: Moirai
system.one_liner: a cost-optimization framework that analyzes job and data access patterns to jointly place data and schedule jobs across hybrid on-premises/cloud deployments

content.subject: how Moirai's Spinner/Allotter/Enacter pipeline turns job-data access logs into updated job-scheduling and data-placement plans

elements.name: Job Queue
elements.role: holds pending jobs (shown as 3,2,1) waiting to be scheduled

elements.name: Job Scheduler
elements.role: routes queued jobs to on-premises or the public cloud and receives updated job plans

elements.name: On-premises
elements.role: local site running jobs 1 and 2 over tables A, B, C, D

elements.name: Public cloud
elements.role: cloud site running job 3 over a replicated copy of table D

elements.name: Spinner
elements.role: builds a job-data graph (jobs and the tables they access) from access logs

elements.name: Jobs (id, resource demand)
elements.role: job nodes 1,2,3 inside the Spinner's graph, weighted by resource demand

elements.name: Tables (id)
elements.role: table nodes A,B,C,D inside the Spinner's graph, linked to the jobs that access them

elements.name: Allotter
elements.role: computes updated job-scheduling and data-placement plans from the job-data graph, current data sizes/placement, replication strategy, cost model, and capacity constraints

elements.name: Data Placement Enacter
elements.role: repartitions and replicates data according to the Allotter's updated data plan

elements.name: Current data sizes and placement
elements.role: Input2 to the Allotter, describing the present data layout

relations.what: queued jobs (3,2,1) are pulled by the scheduler
jobs 2 and 1 are routed to run on-premises
job 3 is routed to run in the public cloud
logs of job and data access are sent to the Spinner
the Spinner emits a job-data graph (Input1) built from jobs and the tables they access
current data sizes and placement feed the Allotter as Input2
an updated job plan is sent back to the Job Scheduler
an updated data plan is sent to the Data Placement Enacter
the enacter repartitions/replicates table D into the public cloud
the enacter updates data partitioning on-premises too

steps.what: the Spinner consumes logs of job and data access to generate a job-data graph of jobs and the tables they touch
steps.carries: logs of job and data access -> job-data graph

steps.what: the Allotter uses the job-data graph plus current data sizes/placement to compute an updated job scheduling policy, sent back to the Job Scheduler
the Allotter likewise computes an updated data-placement plan, sent to the Data Placement Enacter, which repartitions/replicates tables (e.g. replicating D to the public cloud)

values.what: a concrete example placement: jobs 1 and 2 plus tables A,B,C run on-premises, job 3 plus a replicated copy of table D run in the public cloud
values.linked_by: position inside the On-premises/Public-cloud boxes, plus matching numeric/letter IDs shared with the Spinner's job-data graph
values.result_cells: the on-premises and public-cloud boxes show the resulting job/table placement directly, with D shaded pink and linked by a dashed 'replicated' arrow between the two sites

content.key_idea: Moirai periodically turns logs of job and data access into a job-data graph, feeds it and current data placement into a cost-aware Allotter, and pushes updated job-scheduling and data-placement plans back to the Job Scheduler and Enacter.
content.reading_order: left to right from Job Queue through Job Scheduler to the on-premises/public-cloud placement, then down into Moirai's Spinner, Allotter, and Data Placement Enacter pipeline

dark gray text and chip-icon accents on the job/table graph nodes
bright cyan accents on the Allotter's gear/lightning icon and the small chip icons

style.background: white, with a tan band enclosing the Moirai pipeline
style.stroke: thin black arrows for control/data flow; dashed gray arrow for the 'replicated' link between sites
style.arrows: thin black arrows throughout, chevron-style block arrows from the Job Scheduler to each site, and one dashed curved arrow marking replication
style.font: sans-serif (Arial), bold red for the Step 1/2a/2b callouts, bold black for component names

encoding.color_means: blue marks the Job Scheduler; green marks the Spinner; orange marks the Allotter; purple marks the Data Placement Enacter; pink singles out table D as the item replicated between on-premises and the public cloud
encoding.line_style_means: solid black arrows carry jobs, logs, graphs, and plans between components; a dashed gray arrow specifically marks D's replication from on-premises to the public cloud
encoding.state_means: not applicable in the FSM sense; the figure shows one pass of a periodically repeated optimization cycle rather than a persistent state machine
encoding.marker_means: bold red 'Step 1', 'Step 2a', 'Step 2b' labels order the optimization cycle: graph generation, then two parallel plan updates
encoding.emphasis: the tan background box isolates Moirai's own three components (Spinner, Allotter, Data Placement Enacter) from the pre-existing Job Queue/Scheduler and the on-premises/public-cloud deployment it optimizes
reusable_patterns: a components-plus-numbered-step diagram where a worked routing/placement example (numbered jobs, lettered tables) sits directly above the abstract pipeline that produced it
weaknesses: the small circled 1/2/3 job-ID labels next to the Job Scheduler's arrows visually resemble the red Step 1/2a/2b markers but encode a different thing (which job, not which step), which could be misread as one numbering scheme

evidence: The Job Scheduler collects data access logs that record executed jobs, the tables accessed, and the size of data accessed
The Spinner uses collected data to generate a Job-Data Graph for jobs that occurred since the last optimization round
the Allotter takes it along with resource constraints for on-premises and public cloud environments

summary: Figure 3 walks through Moirai's periodic optimization cycle for placing jobs and data across on-premises and public-cloud sites. Above, a worked example shows the Job Scheduler routing queued jobs 2 and 1 to run on-premises (alongside tables A, B, C) and job 3 to the public cloud, with table D replicated between the two sites. Below, inside Moirai, Step 1 has the Spinner consume logs of job and data access to generate a job-data graph (job id/resource-demand nodes linked to the table id nodes they touch). That graph, together with current data sizes and placement (Input2), feeds the Allotter, which applies a replication strategy, cost model, and capacity constraints to compute updated plans: Step 2a sends an updated job plan back to the Job Scheduler, and Step 2b sends an updated data plan to the Data Placement Enacter, which repartitions and replicates the affected tables.
